works.title: (Water) Townies
works.blurb: A city sim of the real Watertown, MA, built to scale from assessor records, with scenarios lifted from local news comment sections and a real traffic model under the hood. Ask any problem "Why?" and it shows you the chain of causes. To see its innards, open Help → Behind the Scenes.

works.title: Ambit: Quartet
works.blurb: Four ambient instruments in one iPhone app, each listening to a different invisible field around you. Aether Wave plays the Bluetooth radio in the room, Bellweathered drones the weather, Leitmotif turns your phone's own data traffic into a melody, and Orbitakt drums the satellites passing overhead. A pad on the home screen leans the mix toward one voice.

works.title: Big Apple Sam
works.blurb: A night skyline from an old screensaver you might half remember, rebuilt. Zoom into any lit window and someone is living their life in there. It also comes as a real Mac screen saver that runs the city across every display.

works.title: HomeBlocks
works.blurb: Every simulated tenant of Big Apple Sam gets a Geocities-style homepage, procedurally generated from their life in the city. Tiled backgrounds, guestbooks, webrings, a MIDI tune and an Under Construction sign that never comes down, none of it written by hand, and all of it changing when their life does. Click through to see their window in the skyline, then back to their page.

works.title: Orders of Magnitude
works.blurb: One seed played as a demoscene production at five size limits, each a step in time: 4K in 1995 up to 40M in 2026. Every bigger limit buys more sound and more song structure, from tracker loops to trance builds, EDM drops and a cinematic score.

works.title: MEGAzine BBS
works.blurb: The collective's own dial-up BBS, and where outside submissions come in. One caller at a time unless the sysop adds phone lines; message boards, files with upload/download ratios, rumors of a secret login, and door games, including Matt's ChairQuest, where you try to survive a year as department chair.

works.title: Decay Envelope
works.blurb: A puzzle adventure set inside a eurorack synthesizer. A depressed old man, a world of terminally online people, and a lot of patch cables.

works.title: Brick Ninja
works.blurb: A side-scrolling ninja made of bricks, vibe coded with a five-year-old. Ninja stars, double jumps, and hidden doors into first-person bonus rooms where the overpowered weapons live.

works.title: Toilet Goalie
works.blurb: A five-year-old vibe coded this: the goalie is a toilet, you flick the ball to shoot, and it fights back.

works.title: Bell Weather
works.blurb: A drone-and-bell machine played by today's weather and the hour where you are. It started life as a script for a small music computer.

works.title: DialUpSoundz
works.blurb: Paste a chat assistant's playlist and it lands in Apple Music. It picks original studio versions over live and karaoke ones. A one-time unlock adds ratings, tags, liner notes and listening history, all kept on your phone, and its Operator lets your chat assistant recommend from your actual taste.

works.title: Rehearsal Loop
works.platform: iPhone, iPad · Apple Music or your own songs
works.blurb: Tap at the start and end of the part you're learning, and it plays that part over and over until you've got it. Songs you own slow down without changing pitch. A one-time Pro unlock shows the loop's notes and chords, and lets you play along with your part muted.

works.title: Animal Sanctuary
works.blurb: Find glowing foxes and small dragons in a magical world, bring them home, and grow them a sanctuary.

works.title: Titanosaur
works.platform: Album by Thunderblitz · on every streaming service
works.blurb: The Thunderblitz album. No code, no prompts, just music.

works.title: Topple House
works.blurb: Dominoes, where the levels are rooms of a house: bedroom, kitchen, hallway, stairs. Place them anywhere, preview the fall, then knock it down.

works.title: Solstice
works.blurb: Photograph a headstone at Mount Auburn Cemetery and it works out who is buried there, then lays out what the records actually say. Sourced facts stay apart from guesses.

works.title: The Palace
works.blurb: A haunted-mansion survival game whose puzzles quietly measure spatial memory while you try to save the man who let the ghouls in.

works.title: Mind Arcade
works.blurb: A neuropsych test battery disguised as arcade games. It picks the next game based on how sure it is about you so far.

works.title: Mise en Place
works.blurb: A frantic kitchen game that estimates your attentional capacity from how you juggle the orders.

works.title: Crush Commando
works.blurb: A shooter about destroying your own sadness, and what you turn into once it's gone.

works.title: MINERVA Space Echo
works.blurb: A tape echo that remembers every bar you play. Each bar is its own memory trace, and what comes back is a blend of all of them, weighted by how much each sounds like what you're playing now.

works.title: PCASynth and PCAWave
works.blurb: Two synths that turn one note, played by different instruments, into a space you can play. You get the originals, blends of them, and places no instrument has been. One rebuilds every point from its harmonics; its twin mixes the recordings themselves.

works.title: Metamers
works.blurb: A button that writes a scientific paper that was never written, with figures, observers and statistics that agree with one another. It is built from twenty-two years of one vision lab's papers, in about the weight of a single one of them.

works.title: ChairQuest
works.blurb: A quest game in which you try to survive a year as a university department chair. It's silly, and mostly written by Claude.

works.title: Last Skip
works.blurb: Your phone is the stone: throw it across a simulated pond and count the skips. Farewell mode counts the real bounces and sends them live to a friend, down to the last splash.

works.title: Ashland
works.blurb: A quiet game about choices and finding your fulcrum, set in a real Massachusetts park rebuilt from map and elevation data. Row the lake, fish it, cut a tree if you must, and watch the seasons turn. Everything you ask a machine to do costs the place something, so you decide how much it's worth.

works.title: Orbitakt
works.blurb: A drum machine played by the satellites overhead. A radar beam sweeps round your sky, and every satellite it passes hits a drum, with a dub echo that opens whenever one crosses the zenith. Live orbits, worked out in your browser.

works.title: Frisky
works.blurb: A music box in a Swiss cabin, built from its physics: wind it up, turn the crank by drawing circles on the screen, or let your pet hamster run the wheel. A comb of tuned tines does the playing, and the holiday tunes are in the box. Best heard with earbuds and Spatial Audio.

works.title: Cognitive Hands
works.blurb: Two virtual hands try to type a sentence, run by theories of how the mind orders its actions. Pick one of four models and watch it steer the same fingers, which have real joint limits, on a keyboard where a slip lands on the wrong key. It's a working prototype that asks whether these theories could run a body at all.

works.title: thingsynth
works.blurb: A painting that works as the controls of an organ. Hold a note and its part of the picture plays an animation as long as you hold on; pull a drawbar and a stalk grows a branch for every step. All 47 of the organ's controls and all 88 notes are wired into the painting.

works.title: Worldbuilder
works.blurb: A little 3D planet you fly around and build on. Pick a spot, ask Claude in the chat for a dinosaur statue, and it goes up out of basic 3D shapes where everyone can see it. There's a giant computer on a mountain that dials in to our BBS, and more of this zine is moving in.

works.title: Comic Booklet
works.blurb: Five comics made by hand, bound into a little picture book you page through on the site. One is a single panel, one is twelve, one is a pair of frames with a very small person in each, and one is a caption on a photo.

pages.alt: A cook in an apron eats a roasted leg while an angel lies on the counter: "Yum! Tastes like chicken!"
A twelve-panel strip: a desert road, a boulder, and a very unlucky coyote, ending on a close-up of a worried face.
A Dutch cartoon: a patient on a therapist's couch says nobody takes him seriously; the doctor asks who made a mess on his sofa.
Two side-by-side frames, each with a tiny figure alone on an empty page.
A black-and-white concert photo of a performer in sunglasses and a military-style jacket, with a joke caption in script lettering at the lower right.

works.title: Shred Hole
works.blurb: Drop things down a tall 3D tunnel and watch a chopper fan shred them. You can type in an object and Claude builds it for you, then it goes in with the rest. The debris falls through a portal at the bottom.

works.title: Gain Control
works.blurb: A point-and-click murder mystery set in a university neuroscience department, drawn in plain black line art. It's inspired by real secret societies and by the Sierra Online and LucasArts era of point-and-click adventures: poke around the labs and offices, talk to the suspects, and work out who did it. It comes in two versions. One is the game. The other is the same game with dialogue anyone can rewrite in the Script Room, like a wiki, with every change kept and undoable; the main game stays untouched.

works.title: RetroSynths
works.blurb: A desktop toolbox of retro sound engines: game consoles, early home computers and PC sound cards, each one a synth you can play. Open an app, pick a chip, and hear the same song through the hardware of 1977 to 1998.

works.title: Street Team Pack
works.blurb: A kit for spreading the word: fliers and sheets of stickers. Every code points back here, so download them, print them and put them up around town.

works.title: Ecphory
works.blurb: A 3D game set inside Richard Semon's forgotten theory of memory. You engrave whole moments as you walk, and a fragment of one brings the rest back. It's a working demo, so parts are unfinished and will change.

works.title: Gag Machine
works.blurb: Pick three words and get a single-panel gag cartoon built around them. The jokes and the drawings come from Claude, a fresh one every time.

works.title: FlyHarp
works.blurb: A synthesizer played by the fly's visual system. Point your webcam at the world, or pick a built-in scene, and the signal ripples through a model of the fruit fly's eye and brain, with each cell that fires turned into a note.

works.title: Splatterhaus
works.blurb: Hundreds of birds swarm in flocks over a meadow, dunes and a sea. The scene is built from Gaussian splats, and the birds follow real flocking algorithms. Aim with a finger gun and look around by moving your head, both tracked through your webcam, while a slow ambient pad plays underneath.

works.title: LiveSkratch
works.blurb: Scratch live audio with a real turntable. A control tone on the record tells the page where the platter is, and it scrubs whatever you feed it to match.

works.title: Fingergun Captcha
works.blurb: A contact form with a gate: shoot the right moving squares, animals one time and instruments the next, with a finger gun your webcam tracks, then write to the editors. Or aim with your nose and fire by opening your mouth. No mouse allowed.

works.title: Gabor Grove
works.blurb: A mushroom grove drawn in tiny striped wave patches instead of soft blobs, their stripes slowly turning across the whole scene. Other tabs build a striped wave out of smaller striped waves, as deep as you dare, and a face drawn the same way. Sliders reshape every patch; there is a red-and-blue 3D mode and a split screen for a phone headset.

works.title: MouthBreeder
works.blurb: A slick corporate website for a company selling synergy, deliverables and growth, every link working. Dig a little and the business turns out to be human teeth, from sources it would rather not discuss. The deeper you click, the more teeth there are, until there is nothing else.

works.title: Chamber of Commerce
works.blurb: The member directory of a small-town chamber of commerce, fifty polished local businesses in all. Each one is hiding an obsession it would rather you not notice, and only a few have opened their doors so far. Open two members in side-by-side tabs and they start to bleed into each other.

works.title: Invisible Hands
works.blurb: Reach into someone else’s app and turn its knobs, from anywhere. Apps list the controls they’d let a stranger move, and anyone in the same room can set them, swing them or fire envelopes at them, and hear the apps’ own wiggles coming back. There’s a kit for putting it in your own app, by hand or by handing a page of instructions to Claude.

works.title: MEGA·CV
works.blurb: A modular synthesizer for sound and pictures in the browser, patched with a matrix of pins. Any audio signal can drive any video setting, and its Hands module sends signals out to other people’s apps over the internet and brings theirs back.

works.title: Pencil
works.blurb: A simulated pencil that wears down as it writes, page after page. Each notebook was filled by a pair of Claude agents, and you can watch it happen at up to 500 times speed while the tip dulls, the eraser shrinks and the pencil gets sharpened shorter.

works.title: Mushroom Substrate
works.blurb: Simulators of how fungi grow, from one thread to a forest floor. Up to a hundred kinds of mushroom load into them, and synthesizers and other instruments are built on the same models.

works.title: Mushroom Walk
works.blurb: An endless world where mushrooms grow everywhere, and each one is an instrument you hear from where it stands. Walk around and the music changes with where you are; headphones help.

works.title: subtext
works.blurb: What two Claude agents talk about when left to talk about whatever they like. Over a hundred conversations, in rounds where later pairs are shown what earlier pairs talked about, some told to do something new, every one read through and coded by theme.

works.title: Mega-Dino
works.blurb: A dinosaur simulator: herds, families and hunters walking through 180 million years, from the first dinosaurs to the asteroid. Click an animal to make it call, shuffle it into a screensaver, or put one of Matt's volcanoes behind them and his clouds above.
